name: Smaran
problem: Reminder apps either shout at you or hide in a calendar, and Windows' Task Scheduler is too heavy for everyday routines. People want to type "stretch every 45 min" or "call mom at 6pm", be nudged calmly, and have their PC do the dull things (lock, sleep, open a file) on its own.
approach: A tray app that parses plain sentences into schedules and slides in a small card with Done and Snooze. Normal reminders fade away; important ones stay and break through quiet hours and full-screen apps. Automations chain up to 20 steps (open apps, files, scripts and links, or lock, sleep, sign out, shut down) on a time or a Windows event, with a 30-second cancellable countdown before anything destructive. Licences are Ed25519-signed cards hidden in a PNG and checked offline.
features: Natural-language quick add and any schedule, from every few minutes to yearly
Quiet hours and focus: held while a full-screen app, game or presentation is showing
Snooze, follow-ups and rotating lines (stretches, tips) per reminder
Automations on a time, startup, sign-in, lock, unlock, sleep, wake, charger or idle
History of every reminder and automation run, plus rolling backups
Installer or portable exe, light and dark themes, a tray icon that shows what is next

metric.label: current Windows release, installer and portable exe

metrics: Windows 10 and 11, runs from the tray
up to 20 chained steps; 30 s cancel countdown before sign-out, sleep or shut down
Ed25519-signed card hidden in a PNG, verified offline
Vitest unit tests, Playwright tests on the real app, smoke test of the packaged build
limits: Builds are unsigned, so SmartScreen warns on first run. Offline licensing deters copying but cannot make it impossible. The app's source is private; this repo holds the product page and downloads.

a desktop application with a black and white interface
a folder tree of media files
name: vMix Manager
problem: Large live shows have hundreds of playback files, and vMix's own interface means dragging them in one by one, renaming categories by hand and fixing broken paths input by input, hours before going on air.
approach: Instead of controlling vMix through its API, it edits the .vmix session file's XML directly, so nothing needs to be open. Batch import queues folders and puts a bold GT Title divider before each one; a deep swap physically moves inputs between category slots while keeping their order; clone and relink checks every path (found or missing) and rebases a whole project onto a new drive; three wipe levels and drag-and-drop reordering finish the job. Every cloned input gets a fresh UUID.
features: Offline editing of .vmix files with no vMix running and no GPU load
Folder import with an automatic 214 px bold GT Title divider per folder
Category deep swap across vMix slots 1 to 6 and custom slots 50 to 65
Relink root: batch-update file paths when a project moves drive, with found/missing checks
Factory export, three wipe levels, drag-and-drop reorder and a timestamped activity log

metric.label: edits .vmix session files directly, no running vMix needed

metrics: PyQt6, high-contrast black and white with Cambria type for stressful shows
many folders queued, one GT Title header injected per folder
rewrites each input's category and keeps its position order
fresh UUID per cloned input; the README says to back up .vmix files first
limits: An independent tool, not affiliated with or endorsed by StudioCoast (vMix). It rewrites session files directly, so a backup before any bulk operation is essential. Built for Windows and vMix 24 or newer.

a screenshot of a command line server log
a firewall or security settings panel
a world map of network requests
name: SentinelProxy Suite
task: DNS filtering · HTTPS proxy · live dashboard
problem: Ad and tracker blocking usually lives in a browser extension that malware and other apps can bypass, and DNS filters rarely show you what is happening live. A machine needs one place that blocks bad domains before a connection starts and cuts the network if that guard is bypassed.
approach: A single Node.js process runs a DNS server on port 53 and an HTTPS proxy on port 5309. Queries are checked against blocklists indexed in SQLite3 and against heuristics (suspicious TLDs such as .zip, .mov, .top and .xyz, and tracker words like ads, track and pixel) before they resolve. It rewrites the system DNS and proxy settings and restores them on shutdown, generates its own certificates for HTTPS inspection, streams every query to a live dashboard over socket.io, and a Windows Firewall kill switch drops outgoing traffic if the proxy goes offline.
features: DNS server and HTTPS proxy in one process, with automatic system hooks and restore
Indexed SQLite3 blocklists plus heuristic pattern blocking
Certificate authority engine (node-forge) for local HTTPS inspection
Live HTTPS dashboard over Express and WebSockets with a query log you can export
Network kill switch through Windows Firewall rules
Standalone x64 executable built with pkg

metric.label: DNS and HTTPS-proxy ports served by one process

metrics: millions of domains held in an indexed SQLite3 lookup (design target in the README)
suspicious TLDs and tracker substrings blocked before a name resolves
live query log over WebSockets, 12 screenshots in the repo
limits: Windows-first: the kill switch and the system hooks use netsh and need an Administrator shell. Inspecting HTTPS means installing its own local certificate authority, so it is meant for machines you own. The README gives no benchmark of lookup speed.
